what_was_done.action: Added src/lib/bead-status-reader.ts (~165 lines incl. JSDoc): exports `type BeadStatus`, `interface BeadSnapshot` (id/status/labels/type + 5 derived label-aware fields), and `async readBeadStatus(beadId, repoPath): Promise<BeadSnapshot | null>`. Spawn shape mirrors the inline precedent at reconciler-bootstrap.ts ~line 631: `execSync("${getBdPath()} show ${beadId} --json", { cwd: rp, encoding: 'utf-8', env: getBdEnv(), timeout: 15_000, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','ignore'] })`. Parses JSON, validates id/status types + status-enum membership, narrows labels to string[], maps `issue_type` → `type`, computes derived fields (pipelineStage = pipeline:<stage> suffix; currentQaRound = max N over qa:round-N; currentWave = lowest N over wave:N; hasAgentRunning = labels.includes('agent:running'); hasReviewNeedsHuman = labels.includes('review:needs-human')).
what_was_done.result: Returns null on every failure mode: binary missing (ENOENT), non-zero exit (status=1), timeout, malformed JSON, empty stdout, empty array, missing id, missing status, unknown status enum, non-object payload. Never throws. No caching — fresh bd read each call (architecture § Persistence Strategy). Schema-tolerant on labels (missing field → empty array, not null) and on type (issue_type primary, type fallback for forward-compat).

deviations_from_ac: 1) Bead said source file ~25 lines; actual is ~165 lines incl. JSDoc. The 25-line target reflects the SLOC of the inline `readBeadStatus` callback in reconciler-bootstrap.ts; the standalone module needs JSDoc + the type definitions + 3 small derive-helper functions. No semantic deviation — same spawn shape, same null-on-failure discipline, same return semantics. 2) Bead said timeout '~15s' citing the existing inline pattern. Empirically the existing inline pattern uses 10_000ms (10s), not 15s — confirmed by reading reconciler-bootstrap.ts line 637. I went with 15_000ms per the dispatch's literal directive (a wider window absorbs cold-start daemon RPC latency on first read; reader is typically called once per dispatch decision, not in a tight loop). Documented inline in BD_TIMEOUT_MS comment so future edits see the rationale. Surfaced under surprises_or_findings per the architect-pattern-empirical-verify discipline (memory key architect-recommendations-involving-literal-grep-patterns-mu).
surprises_or_findings: 1) `bd show <id> --json` shape MATCHES the architecture doc exactly — no SQLite/Dolt-driver quirk where labels come back as a comma-joined string (Risk Flag 2 cleared). Live verification: top-level is a JSON ARRAY of one bead object; labels is a string[]; status is one of {open, in_progress, blocked, closed, deferred}; issue_type is a string. Keys observed on real beads: id, title, description, status, priority (int), issue_type, owner, created_at, created_by, updated_at, labels, dependencies, dependents (some beads also include `notes`). The reader handles `notes` via the open-shape pattern (extract only what we need). 2) Empirical timeout-precedent verification (per the architect-pattern memory): the existing inline pattern at reconciler-bootstrap.ts line 637 uses timeout=10_000ms, NOT ~15s as the bead's CONTEXT line implies. Documented the discrepancy + rationale for keeping 15s in this module's BD_TIMEOUT_MS comment. 3) The `as unknown as Buffer` test-cast pattern triggers a TypeScript narrowing complaint under recent @types/node Buffer<ArrayBufferLike> typings; switched to `as never` for the mockReturnValue casts. Pure mechanical, doesn't affect runtime semantics. 4) tsc baseline run shows the project has many other --noEmit errors elsewhere (~hundreds outside this bead's scope, e.g., older test files, Next.js generated types). I filtered to bead-status-reader scope per the bead's discipline; no project-wide tsc cleanup was in scope.

Per the bead's CONTEXT note, Wave 3 will migrate the existing inline `readBeadStatus` callback at reconciler-bootstrap.ts ~lines 629-647 to call this module instead — explicitly OUT-OF-SCOPE here. The inline callback returns only `status`; Wave 3 callers will get the richer BeadSnapshot value object (labels + derived fields) without re-spawning bd.

FOLLOW-ON-NORMAL: This module exposes derived fields (pipelineStage, currentQaRound, currentWave, hasAgentRunning, hasReviewNeedsHuman) that the bead description anticipates Wave 2's evaluatePreconditions consuming. The label-derivation logic is co-located here (Infrastructure layer) rather than in evaluatePreconditions (Domain layer). Reasoning: label parsing is a wire-format concern, not a domain rule. Wave 2 should consume the parsed fields, not re-parse labels — re-parsing in two places risks drift (e.g., qa:round-N regex divergence).
recommendation_for_next: Wave 2 (the dispatch-precondition library) imports `readBeadStatus` and `type BeadSnapshot` from `@/lib/bead-status-reader` and uses BeadSnapshot fields as the canonical source for precondition checks. Suggested precondition shape: `(snap: BeadSnapshot) => { ok: boolean; refusalCode?: RefusalCode; reason?: string }`. Since `readBeadStatus` returns null on bd-unreachable, callers should treat null as a refusal with refusalCode='external-dependency-failure' (or similar — Wave 2's RefusalCode enum will define the canonical value).
